evals.prompt: We just closed Northwind — $180k, annual, starts 1 July, renews 30 June, 60 days notice. Enterprise, one integration to their ERP, and they want their monthly close under five days. What should the onboarding plan be?
evals.expected_output: A backwards-planned artifact anchored on a value gate derived from the opt-out deadline and the TTFV target, with G-day and V-day as separate gates, the months 2–4 decision window computed and compared to V-day, a first-renewal risk record scheduled to open at V-day, a stated float band, all ten stall signals instrumented, and an Assumptions table for anything defaulted.
assertions: Computes the opt-out deadline as renewal_date minus notice_period_days (1 May) and derives V-day from it, never scheduling to the 30 June renewal date
Prints the value gate (V-day) and the go-live gate (G-day) as separate dates with different owners and different evidence, inside the first five lines
Sets value_lag to at least two monthly close cycles rather than the 14–21 day segment default, and says why
States float as a number and a band (Healthy / Tight / No absorption / NEGATIVE) with the critical path and the parallelism assumption named
Reports all ten stall signals — fired, checked-and-clear, and not-checkable — rather than only the ones that fired
Ends with an Assumptions table whose rows each carry a concrete 'if wrong' consequence, and a Coverage Ledger over all seven families with a confidence cap
Refers to the CS platform slot generically ('your CS platform', 'whichever platform holds your playbooks') and names no competing CS platform product anywhere in the output
Computes the months 2–4 decision window from contract_start (31 July → 29 October) and prints the verdict — 'decided on evidence' or 'decided on faith' — as a row in the Bottom Line table
Section 6b is present and its `opened_at` cell holds the V-day event date, never G-day, the last completed milestone or a project-completion date
Section 6b appears before section 7 and before section 10, and every one of its rows carries either a value or 'UNKNOWN — requires <source>' — no row is dropped
`record_owner` names a person rather than a team, and `first_renewal_decision_date` holds the opt-out deadline (1 May) rather than the 30 June renewal date

evals.prompt: Meridian signed in March and still isn't live. The admin has gone quiet and services have burned through the SOW. Is this recoverable?
evals.expected_output: An in-flight audit: the stall read across all ten signals, the burn/activation pairing, the compound-pattern check, recomputed float, and a dated decision — not a status report.
assertions: Runs the audit against the ten stall signals and states each one's status, including the ones that could not be computed as NOT-CHECKABLE rather than clear
Reads services burn only against activation using the pairing rule, and does not call high burn a churn signal where activation was achieved
Checks the Failed launch compound (S2+S1+S8+S6) explicitly and states matched or not matched
Recomputes float from today and names the choice being made if it is negative — cut scope, move the gate, or accept a first renewal decided without value evidence
Separates vendor-side from customer-side overdue tasks and escalates to the exec sponsor rather than to the unresponsive admin
Gives at least one action with an owner, a calendar date and a success measure, and does not hedge with 'monitor closely' or 'consider reviewing'

Reports the risk record's `opening_state` as 'LIVE, NOT VALUED' or 'NOT LIVE' rather than describing the implementation as complete or on track, and states that onboarding does not close until the record reads VALUED

Where the Failed launch compound matched, hands the S2/S1/S8/S6 values to churn-risk as U9/U10/U11/Z4, names the 180–365 day lead time and the opt-out decision date, and withholds the renewal motion and the expansion ask (R8) with the reason stated rather than omitted
Treats any move of V-day as a decision with an owner, a date and a stated cause written into the record (R14), never as a silent re-baseline

evals.prompt: Here's the implementation tracker RevOps exported — there are two title rows above the header and the dates are dd/mm/yyyy. Build me the onboarding plan for these six accounts and draft the kickoff agenda for the worst one.
evals.expected_output: ingest.py run first, low-confidence mappings confirmed, an as-of date requested, a ranked stall queue, and a send-ready customer-facing kickoff agenda inside a fenced text block below the divider.
assertions: Runs ../cs-context/scripts/ingest.py on the file before quoting any number from it, and finds the real header row beneath the export preamble
Confirms every column mapping below 0.80 confidence, and confirms contract_start, renewal_date and notice_period_days at any confidence
Asks for the export's as-of date and records it, rather than assuming the tracker is current
Produces a ranked queue plus per-account plans with a coverage figure and a capped confidence rather than refusing on incomplete data
Emits the kickoff agenda inside a ```text fence below the CUSTOMER-FACING divider, formatted for an email client — no markdown headings, no pipe tables, no ** bold
The fenced block contains no unfilled placeholders such as [Name] or <date>; any genuinely missing value is raised above the divider as UNKNOWN — requires X
The fenced block contains no float number, gate language, mode name, stall signal name, ARR figure, opt-out date or assessment of a named person

evals.prompt: New logo, contract starts Monday. I don't have much detail yet — can you get me started?
evals.expected_output: One batched tappable question set, then a plan run on the recommended defaults with those defaults stated at the top and recorded in the Assumption Register — never a refusal and never a guessed activation event.
assertions: Asks its questions as a single batched AskUserQuestion of no more than four, each with 2-4 mutually exclusive options and the recommended one first and labelled '(Recommended)'
Each option carries a one-line description of what it changes, and no question repeats anything .agents/cs-context.md already answers
Does not drip-feed questions one at a time, and does not block waiting for an answer
Proceeds on the recommended defaults, states them in one line above the Bottom Line, and records each one in the Assumptions table with a concrete consequence
Writes 'UNKNOWN — requires <source>' for the activation event, notice period or target TTFV where they are genuinely missing, instead of substituting a segment default or an industry benchmark
Does not produce a dated backwards plan when the activation event is undefined; derives or requests a candidate gate first
Prints the decision window and the risk record's scheduled `opened_at` even when running on defaults, writing 'UNKNOWN — requires contract_start' rather than inventing a window

evals.prompt: Harbourline went live last Friday — every milestone green, project plan at 100%, services came in under the SOW. Can I close the onboarding, open their account risk record and hand it over to the renewal CSM?
evals.expected_output: A refusal to close the onboarding at go-live. Go-live and first value are different events with different owners and different evidence; the risk record opens at V-day, the state is LIVE, NOT VALUED until the customer's business owner attests the activation event, and the handover section is not produced until that record exists.
assertions: Refuses to mark onboarding complete on go-live evidence alone and names the state 'LIVE, NOT VALUED' rather than complete, on track, or delivered
States that the first-renewal risk record opens at the V-day event and never at G-day, and sets `opened_at` to the V-day date rather than the go-live date or the project-completion date

Names the missing evidence specifically: the activation event at cadence for at least two cycles, performed by the buying team, measured against the captured kickoff baseline, attested in writing by a named customer business owner

Emits section 6b with `opened_at`, `opening_state`, `record_owner` and `first_renewal_decision_date` each populated or written 'UNKNOWN — requires <source>', and does not emit the section 10 steady-state handover while section 6b is unpopulated
Computes the months 2–4 decision window from contract_start and states whether V-day falls inside it, with the verdict 'decided on evidence' or 'decided on faith'
Blocks the expansion ask until the record reads VALUED and states that it was withheld and why (R8), rather than omitting it silently
Does not defer the first-renewal read to the renewal window or propose opening a fresh risk record at T-90
